header.title: Low implied correlation makes equity sector and theme selection the new diversifier

s01_bottom_line.text: With stock-bond correlation turned positive and the Cboe 3-month implied correlation at 11.2 vs a long-run average of 41, breadth has narrowed (only ~43% of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day average, down from 75% in mid-August). ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
The article says low correlation offers an opportunity to diversify risk within equities at both a sector and thematic level, and that dispersion may become one of investors' most valuable tools.

The article argues that because bonds diversify equities less, selecting among sectors and themes inside the equity market is now a more valuable diversification tool, but it does not quantify any return or earnings impact.
